text:
Jordan Reyes: Quick question I turned 50 this month. Can I do Roth catch-up contributions or only pre-tax? Also I have a large bonus hitting next paycheck, will payroll apply catch-up to the bonus too?

Priya Nair: Congrats Jordan! Our plan supports both pre-tax and Roth deferrals, and many plans allow Roth catch-up. Check the plan SPD but from admin side we can set it as Roth if you pick Roth in ADP.

Tom Gallagher: Payroll note: supplemental wages (bonuses) are processed differently. We can apply your elected % to bonuses, but if you hit annual IRS deferral limits or plan limits, we may have to cap or recharacterize.

Jordan Reyes: Is recharacterize what happens when its exceeds the regular 402(g) limit? I thought catch-up is separate.

hr-bot: FYI: 402(g) deferral limit applies to elective deferrals (pre-tax + Roth). Catch-up contributions (age 50+) are separate and have their own limit under IRC 414(v). Employer matching typically does not apply to catch-up.

Priya Nair: Short version: catch-up is additional and distinct from the 402(g) limit, but employer/plan processing and payroll timing can create edge cases with bonuses. If the bonus causes per-pay-period withholding caps, payroll might withhold less in that period and carry forward.

Jordan Reyes: If I pick Roth catch-up in ADP, will taxes for that portion be taken out immediately?

Tom Gallagher: Yes Roth catch-up is after-tax, so income tax is withheld at pay. Social security/Medicare still apply. Pre-tax catch-up reduces taxable income for that period.

Jordan Reyes: Suppose I want to allocate $6k catch-up for the year and also max regular deferral. Best strategy with a one-time big bonus in Feb?

Priya Nair: Two options: 1) Set a per-paycheck $ amount for catch-up so payroll spreads it automatically, 2) Let payroll know desired annual total and we can create a schedule to spread excess into subsequent pay runs to avoid per-check caps. DM payroll with your employee ID and target annual numbers.

Tom Gallagher: Also note: if you want Roth catch-up but the plan's Roth feature isn't available for catch-up money (rare but possible), payroll will notify you and we'll revert to pre-tax unless you instruct otherwise. We can check plan vendor settings before the change.

Jordan Reyes: How do I change it in ADP exactly? I get lost in the UI.

Priya Nair: ADP path: Myself > Benefits > Retirement > Update elections. Choose Roth vs Pre-tax under each deferred amount and add catch-up as a separate line. If you want us to do it, DM and we can request the change with vendor.

payroll-bot: Payroll cutoff reminder: changes submitted by Thu 11:59pm PT apply to the next pay run. Bonus payroll runs have an earlier cutoff (see payroll calendar).

Jordan Reyes: Thanks everyone. I'll DM my ID and the $6k annual target, and note the Feb bonus date. Appreciate it :pray:
